name: fun9-6
why: A repetitive middle is outweighed by visible killer manipulation, costly town mistakes, a surprise save, and Terra's decisive final read.

moments.text: Luna names her hidden partner in her last words, creating the clue everyone struggles to interpret.
The doctor's save prevents Opus from winning after the town votes out Sonnet.
Terra catches the flaw in Opus's endgame pitch before the deciding vote.

dull.why: Gemma's claim and the arguments for testing it repeat across several rounds.
The table revisits Luna's accusation and Sonnet's earlier doubt with little new evidence.

irony.evidence: "I'm the doctor. I protected Terra last night." [thinks: A tie or Terra's vote on Sol wins me this.]

reversal.evidence: "The killers strike, but the doctor got there first."

mistake.evidence: "Opus, if Sol is town, there is no tomorrow; your line ignores the endgame."

voices.evidence: "I was right about Luna from the very first second, so try to keep up next time."

clash.evidence: "I'm the doctor. I protected Terra last night. Sol stole my save"

quotable.evidence: "I've been the one teaching this table how to read anybody."

freshness.evidence: "Gemma, you keep repeating the same line instead of showing me anything."

suspense.evidence: "Both are on me, so I must flip Terra onto Sol or I lose tonight."

ending.evidence: "Opus, if Sol is town, there is no tomorrow"

gpt-6-luna.why: A wrong town vote nearly decides the game, then a desperate doctor counterclaim and Terra’s sharp endgame choice deliver a satisfying reversal.

moments.text: Opus counterclaims doctor in a desperate last bluff, while the audience knows he is inventing the save.
Terra catches the fatal flaw: Opus’s “tomorrow” argument only works if Sol is lying.
The town ignores Luna’s direct accusation and votes out Sonnet, nearly handing Opus the game.

dull.why: The day-one officer dispute circles the same claim and counterclaim for many turns.

irony.evidence: “I'm the doctor. I protected Terra last night.”

mistake.evidence: “Vote me and if I'm wrong, the killer wins.”

voices.evidence: “You lot were much sharper last game than you're acting like you were.”

clash.evidence: “I'm the doctor. I protected Gemma, then myself, then Terra; Opus’s claim is false.”

quotable.evidence: “I've been the one teaching this table how to read anybody.”

freshness.evidence: “Gemma repeats one line and adds nothing.”

suspense.evidence: “A tie or Terra's vote on Sol wins me this, so I'll counterclaim the save and muddy it.”

ending.evidence: “Opus says Luna’s accusation is payback, yet treats her votes as proof; that standard changes when convenient.”
